questions.question: Explain why water is the most important natural reason for the location of settlements, with South African examples.
questions.expected_answer: People, animals and crops all need a reliable supply of water, and water is also needed for industry. So settlements grew beside rivers, such as Vereeniging and Parys on the Vaal River and Upington on the Orange River, and around springs, such as Bloemfontein and Kuruman. Places where rivers could be crossed, called drifts, also attracted settlements. Today dams and pipelines bring water to places such as Gauteng.

questions.question: Explain how climate and vegetation affect where people live in South Africa.
questions.expected_answer: People prefer a pleasant climate with enough rain, and since South Africa's rainfall decreases from east to west, more people live in the wetter east than in the dry west. The winter rainfall south-western Cape suits grapes, wheat and fruit, so farming towns like Paarl and Worcester grew there. Grasslands provided grazing for cattle, forests provided timber, as at Knysna, and in the sparse Karoo, farms are large and towns far apart.

questions.question: Describe three other natural features that influence the location of settlements.
questions.expected_answer: Flat land is easier to build on and farm, and river valleys have fertile soil. Sheltered bays make good harbours, so Cape Town grew at Table Bay and Durban around its natural bay, and towns with port in their names show this. Mountain passes allow roads through mountains, so towns grow nearby, and long ago people settled on hills that were easier to defend, such as Mapungubwe Hill.
